Package dev.opencollab.paletter

Class Palette

java.lang.Object
dev.opencollab.paletter.Palette
public final class Palette extends Object
Everything a Bedrock client of one version needs to know about items and blocks: vanilla data plus a stack of PaletteLayers, compiled. Build one with Paletter; extend(PaletteLayer) adds a layer.

Thread safety: a palette is immutable and safe to share between threads and sessions. Its lazily built caches (behaviour, version indexes) and extend(PaletteLayer) synchronize internally; no method needs external locking.

Null handling: parameters and return values are @NonNull unless the signature says @Nullable. Lookups by identifier, NBT or runtime id return null where nothing matches. Methods that take a key (blockDefinition, runtimeId, resolve) throw IllegalArgumentException for a key this palette does not contain (e.g. a custom block of a layer it lacks); their orElse overloads return the default instead. Nothing throws for data a client sent.

Vocabulary: keys (BedrockBlockState, BedrockItemVariant, ...) identify content independent of any version; definitions (RegisteredBlockState, RegisteredItem) are what the palette sends to the client; resolutions (ResolvedBlock, ResolvedItem) are what a palette makes of a key: the definition, whether a fallback was used, and the behaviour values.

Sending it to a client: 


 palette.applyTo(session.getCodecHelper());     // item and block definitions for the codec
 palette.applyTo(startGamePacket);              // block properties and the block network id mode
 session.sendPacket(palette.voxelShapesPacket());   // always, before start game
 session.sendPacket(palette.itemComponentPacket());
 session.sendPacket(palette.creativeContentPacket());
Translating content uses handles, version independent and interned objects (BedrockBlockState, BedrockItemVariant): blockState(NbtMap, Lookup) and itemVariant(String, int, Lookup) find them once, then runtimeId(BedrockBlockState) and blockDefinition(BedrockBlockState) for blocks, resolve(ItemKey) for items. encode(dev.opencollab.paletter.item.BedrockItemStack) and decode(org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.inventory.ItemData) translate whole stacks at the protocol boundary. They are field reads and array lookups that do not allocate. The ids behind the handles are not API.
Since:
1.0.0

    • resolve

      public @NonNull ResolvedBlock resolve(@NonNull BedrockBlockState state)
      What this palette sends for a block state and what that does: the definition (fallbacks applied, as blockDefinition(BedrockBlockState)), whether a fallback was used, and its behaviour values (friction, destroy time, collision shape, light, ...): palette.resolve(state).behaviour().get(BlockBehaviour.FRICTION). Vanilla values come from the bundled captures of the palette's version, custom ones from their components. Behaviour is only reachable through a resolution, so the palette that resolved it is the one that answers.

      A resolution is made once per state and kept by the palette, so a lookup allocates nothing. Compare resolutions with equals.

      Parameters:
      state - the block state, a key
      Returns:
      the resolution of the state
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - like blockDefinition(BedrockBlockState). Use resolve(BedrockBlockState, ResolvedBlock) for states that may be missing
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • blockOf

      public @Nullable BedrockBlockState blockOf(@NonNull ItemKey key)
      The block an item variant is sent with in this palette's version, in its default state, as a key: a BedrockBlockState, for every kind of variant (vanilla, extra, custom block items, fallbacks). Paletter alone decides it. A stack may carry a block state of its own, see encode(dev.opencollab.paletter.item.BedrockItemStack). blockDefinition(blockOf(variant)) is what is sent, and resolve(variant).block() the same without the key. It follows the palette: the fallback's block in an old version, the custom block of a layer. runtimeId(BedrockBlockState) gives its runtime id here.
      Parameters:
      key - the item type or variant
      Returns:
      the block's key, or null if the item is not a block item here (or no state of the newest data resolves to the block, see blockState(BlockDefinition))
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • resolve

      public @Nullable ResolvedItem resolve(@NonNull ItemKey key)
      What this palette sends for an item variant, without building an ItemData: the item definition, damage and block of encode(dev.opencollab.paletter.item.BedrockItemStack) (fallbacks applied), as one cached record. For the variants of the newest version it is a field read and an array load, it does not allocate. Use it to read the definition or damage of many items; a stack's own block state, count and NBT are not part of it. ResolvedItem.fallback() tells whether the variant is sent as another item, ResolvedItem.variant() which.
      Parameters:
      key - the item type or variant
      Returns:
      the resolution, or null if the item does not exist in this version and has no fallback
      Since:
      1.0.0

      public @Nullable BedrockBlockState blockState(@NonNull org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.definitions.BlockDefinition definition)
      The key of a block this palette sends: its exact state, else the first state that resolves to it (several states may share a fallback). For a definition of this palette, blockDefinition(blockState(definition)) is the definition again. The block is looked up by runtime id, the hash of its state: a definition of another palette gives the key of the block with the same runtime id here, as this palette knows it (a custom block of this palette's own layer).

      Returns:
      the key, or null if this palette has no block with the definition's runtime id, no state resolves to it, or the definition is not a RegisteredBlockState

    • encode

      public @NonNull org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.inventory.ItemData encode(@NonNull BedrockItemStack stack)
      Encodes a stack for this palette's version: the item with the aux value, count and NBT, and the block the stack places (its own block state if it has one and the item places blocks, else the item's default block). An item this version does not have, or this palette does not know at all (an identifier nobody registered), is replaced by the same stand-in: the item's fallback, else the default one of the Fallbacks (minecraft:unknown unless configured otherwise), whichever way the item is looked up.
      Parameters:
      stack - the stack, built from keys
      Returns:
      the item data, or ItemData.AIR only if there is neither a fallback for the item nor a default one (Fallbacks.NONE)
      Since:
      1.0.0

      Decodes a stack the client sent. The block state is set only if the stack's block differs from the item's default block. The stack of a fallback shared by several variants, or of an item that is not a variant of the newest version, is not recognized.
      Parameters:
      data - the stack as the client sent it
      Returns:
      the stack, or null for air or an item this palette cannot identify
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • sameStack

      public boolean sameStack(@NonNull org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.inventory.ItemData a, @NonNull org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.inventory.ItemData b)
      Whether two stacks are the same stack of items as far as this palette can tell: the same item definition, damage, count, NBT, canPlace, canBreak, blocking ticks and block. The net id is not part of it.

      Definitions compare by identity, as in Cloudburst (ItemData#equals, which also ignores the block). A definition that is not this palette's own instance (another palette's, or Geyser's own) is first mapped to this palette's entry of the same identifier and runtime id, so a stack of a base palette matches the same stack of a palette extending it. A definition this palette does not have matches only itself. The same goes for block definitions. A missing NBT tag and an empty one are the same, so are missing and empty block lists.

      Stacks that differ only in count, or only in NBT, never match.

      Parameters:
      a - the first stack
      b - the second stack
      Returns:
      true if the stacks are the same
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • extend

      public @NonNull Palette extend(@NonNull PaletteLayer layer)
      Compiles one more layer on top of this palette, e.g. for one session. Concurrent calls for one layer return the same palette, though each may compile it. The result is cached while it is reachable.

      A layer that cannot be compiled (a duplicate identifier or runtime id, across or within layers, a block hash collision, an exception from a component encoder or a callback) throws a PaletteException naming the layer and the content identifier. This palette is unchanged then, and no palette or failure is cached: the same layer throws again, and other layers can still be applied.

      Parameters:
      layer - the layer to add
      Returns:
      the palette with the layer
      Throws:
      PaletteException - if the layer cannot be compiled
